primary_activity: A single occupant sleeps, dresses, and starts the day at a compact north-window work and grooming surface.
secondary_activities: Read briefly in a separate armchair
Store clothing in a south-side wardrobe
Keep a phone, lamp, or book on one reachable bedside surface
circulation_plan: The east-south door opens into a clear central landing. The main route follows the east side of the bed toward the north desk, with a shorter branch west to the armchair; the bed's accessible long side and desk chair pull-back area stay open.
spatial_organization: The bed runs along the west wall rather than floating centrally. A narrow desk occupies the north wall under the window, wardrobe storage anchors the south-west wall, and a small reading pocket uses the quiet south-east corner.
daylight_or_opening_considerations: The north window gives the desk morning light, while the bed remains outside its clearance. The east-south door requires an uncluttered arrival zone and prevents wardrobe placement on the east wall.
intended_furniture_groups: bed and one nightstand as a restrained sleep group
desk and chair as a north-window morning work/grooming group
armchair and side table as a separate reading group
intended_open_space: A central-east L-shaped circulation zone from door to desk and bed side, plus a clear pull-out strip behind the desk chair and approach space in front of wardrobe.
difference_from_previous_scenes: Conceived independently after scene2: this bedroom uses one bedside surface, a north-window desk, an east reading pocket, and a west-wall bed; it is not a mirrored or centered bed/wardrobe arrangement.
